title: Quel’Delar: The Broken Blade Restored
summary: A broken blade carries a kingdom’s sacrifice into a search for restoration. Rival heirs, the darkness of Icecrown and the Sunwell’s light shape what the living may inherit.
opening: A battered hilt survives beneath the northern cold. Before Quel’Delar can be whole again, its seekers must learn whose hope it once carried and what darkness has entered the steel.

chapters.title: The battered hilt
chapters.body:
From the dangers of the Frozen Halls came a battered hilt, the remnant of a blade whose history had not ended with its breaking. At Quel’Delar’s Rest, the Silver Covenant and Sunreavers took up the question it carried. Before the sword could be made whole, its surviving fragment had drawn rival heirs toward an inheritance neither could leave forgotten.

Caladis Brightspear received seekers of the Silver Covenant; Myralion Sunblaze received those of the Sunreavers. Their allegiances opened different roads through Dalaran. Old kinship between high elves and blood elves could not settle who should hold the blade. Above the city’s violet heights, the hope of restoration stood beside a rivalry over the memory it would carry.

At Wyrmrest Temple, Krasus lent the seekers a history of the ancient blade. Kalecgos questioned whether mortals should command such power; the dragons knew the grief of a mighty weapon turned against them. Alexstrasza permitted the search to continue. Beneath the red-bronze shrine, the hilt’s past began to emerge as both a promise and a warning.

In Dalaran, Caladis and Myralion each directed the search among their own people. Both sought the old blade’s restoration, yet their purposes did not make them one council. Beneath the city’s pale towers and violet enchantments, a shared inheritance remained contested. Each hoped the sword would return to hands worthy of the history their people remembered.

A disguise opened the way to guarded knowledge. Suspicion and old allegiances stood around the history of the dragonforged blades, and the seeker recovered it under a borrowed appearance. The pages offered something steel alone could not restore. Before the broken hilt could become a weapon again, its name and the burden of its past had to be understood.

chapters.title: A blade remembered
chapters.body:
The recovered history gave the hilt a name: Quel’Delar, sister to Quel’Serrar. Its past bound the red dragonflight’s craft to the high elven crown and a defender who stood before the Sunwell. A gift had endured beyond a kingdom’s wound. Yet remembering the blade did not settle who might bear it next, or how its broken length could be restored.

In the older memory, Alexstrasza gave the blade to Anasterian, who later entrusted it to Thalorien Dawnseeker. The gift passed from a dragon to a king and onward to a defender. Quel’Thalas’s fate would test the inheritance. Beside the Sunwell’s ancient light, the sword’s promise waited upon the courage of the hand that carried it.

During the Third War, the Scourge reached Quel’Thalas. Thalorien held the approach before the Sunwell and fell buying time for those behind him. His defense could not spare the kingdom its wound, but his name remained bound to the blade he bore. Long afterward, another search would seek to restore what had survived that loss.

At Quel’Delar’s Rest, Lana’thel brought a darker memory. After Thalorien’s fall, the sword had passed into her hands. As the Lich King’s servant, she was ordered to destroy it. She carried Quel’Delar north and broke it there. A knight’s last defense and a queen’s enslavement now met in the shattered steel lying beneath the snow.

The breaking had not ended Quel’Delar’s history. Myralion vowed that the Sunreavers would restore it, while Caladis led the Silver Covenant’s separate search. Their resolve gave purpose to the work ahead. The blade had to be remade, the will within it faced, and the touch left by the Scourge cleansed. Beyond the hilt’s recovery waited a more perilous restoration.

chapters.title: Make the blade whole
chapters.body:
In the Pit of Saron, infused bars and a forgehammer joined the blade’s broken length. The mine lay beneath Icecrown, a place of forced labor and dark ore within the frozen land. Quel’Delar became whole again. Yet the material that held its pieces carried a peril of its own, and the restored weapon had not been freed from the darkness around its making.

The joined blade was carried to the Crucible of Souls within the Forge of Souls. There it was tempered amid the machinery of the Lich King’s frozen halls. The weapon had regained its shape, but its next passage would expose a deeper difficulty. An edge made whole could still bear a spirit that had not been cleansed.

Quel’Delar pressed its bearer toward the Halls of Reflection. The blade possessed a will, and its command led into the Lich King’s chamber. Within the blue-black hall, the search for restoration became a struggle for mastery. A finished edge could be carried in the hand; the power directing that hand now had to be confronted.

The seeker resisted Quel’Delar’s command and brought its will to heel. The sword survived the struggle, yet restraint did not make it pure. Icecrown’s dark ore still held the repaired steel together. A voice within the chamber would name what the reforging had carried into it, and the search would turn from mastery toward cleansing.

Uther’s spirit named the deeper wound: saronite was the blood of an Old God, and its taint had entered the restored blade. His counsel turned the seeker toward the Sunwell. Beyond Icecrown’s frozen halls lay older light, in a sacred place the blood elves had reclaimed. There the sword might be cleansed of what its new forging had forced into it.

chapters.title: Light and inheritance
chapters.body:
At Quel’Danas, Halduron Brightwing refused entry to the sacred place the blood elves had recently reclaimed. The Sunwell’s shores carried the memory of a kingdom nearly lost. Before the dangerous blade could reach its light, the seeker had to earn trust. Beyond the Dead Scar, the journey approached those whose duty was to guard that inheritance.

At Thalorien’s resting place, the seeker faced a trial and the memory of the fallen knight. His death remained in the Third War, yet his blessing could reach the bearer who now carried his blade. The past had not returned him to life. It offered a bond between the defender’s sacrifice and the burden of restoring what had survived him.

At last, the tempered blade was lowered into the Sunwell. Its light cleansed the saronite taint, and Quel’Delar emerged purified. Thalorien’s sacrifice and Lana’thel’s enslavement remained part of its history. What changed was the inheritance the living could carry. Broken and remade, the sword left the sacred waters free of the darkness that had entered its steel.

The restored blade returned toward Dalaran along the paths of the Silver Covenant and Sunreavers. Each people could welcome the recovery without ending the rivalry around its inheritance. Among the blood elves, Aethas could present a new bearer. Yet no single name settled the sword’s future for all. Quel’Delar’s long passage through gift, sacrifice and corruption had reached the hope of restoration.

reviewNote: Research story with secondary quest transcripts and a secondary mirror of an archived Blizzard article. Original Wrath 3.3.5a quest text, relative flashback dates, and faction variants need client comparison and editor review. Randomized loot is a gameplay trigger; Alliance and Horde lines are alternatives; Thalorien’s historical death is distinct from his later quest test; no named adventurer is canonical. Generated art is interpretive; in-client area/model resemblance review remains open.
